name: Cyclonian
objectiveText: Bring the items on Bath'rah's Parchment to Bath'rah the Windwatcher in Alterac. Liferoot  ( 8 ) Bloodscalp Tusk  ( 30 ) Essence of the Exile  ( 1 )

comments.body:
You create the Essence of the Exile by collecting these items from elementals in Arathi Highlands:

https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=4479 - Burning Charm (8)
https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=4481 - Cresting Charm (8)
https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=4480 - Thundering Charm (8).

Once you have them, right click the cauldron near Bath'Rah, and you will receive the Essence of the Exile.
replies: Thanks, this is the info I came for and you presented it very well.

comments.body:
The elementals needed are found in Arathi Highlands as mentioned. There are 3 different druid rings, or stonehenges for that matter, that you need to go to.

The 4th, and southmost, contains earth elementals that you do NOT NEED. Go to the others and get the burning, crescent and thundering charms of the elementals. Need 8 of each !

This part of the quest is NOT soloable at 30 or the low 30's. The elementals are pretty tough even when you're equal level with them. Get a friend to help or use an alt char. thats 40+ to farm them easily.

The Bloodscalp tusks you find at the Bal'lal ruins north of Grom'gol (sp?) (Horde outpost in Stranglethorne anyways). Follow the beach north out of the camp, and swim around any crocs to get there safely.

I tried this part myself at 30 and found it very difficult and slow going. You need 30 tusks and the drop rate is rather crappy, so takes quite a few trolls to get them all. I left out of boredom and getting killed a bit too often, then returned at 32 and killed them relatively easy. Short break to get health up between each kill. Best way to get the tusks is to NOT pull the ones inside the ruins (if you are solo anyhow) but follow around the outskirt of the ruins. There are trolls located all the way around the ruins, and these are all single-pulls and lvl 33-34, mix of shaman, axe throwers and warrios. Shamans being the beotch of the three with their flame blast ~_~

Anyhow, hope this helps... I'm off to turn in the quest and try for the last part... probably die, but hey, thats what warriors do best.. right?

Good luck and have fun !

Karzumk, Freelancing Warrior of 32 levels (and rising !) ~Aszune Server~

Tricky, but can be done starting in the mid-30's.

The trolls you need to harvest the tusks from are only Level 33 and 34, but they are hard to pull from each other. The drop rate was low, took roughly an hour and a half to get the 30 tusks required (probably about 200 kills). The Shaman are very nasty and almost brought me down as a Level 36 several times just soloing.

The crests can either be harvested in Arathi Highlands via an alternate, or purchased at the AH.  They aren't necessarily a quest item, so they aren't soulbound. Burning Exiles located at the West Circle of Binding, Cresting (Water) Exiles at the one to the North-northeast of Refuge Point, and Thundering Exiles east of Refuge. Make sure you don't accidentally use the charms on the other exiles. Save them.

Liferoot can be found on the Kurzen Medicine Men (Level 33, Caster/Paladin type mobs) located just east after entering STV from the north. You can also purchase it very cheaply at the AH.

You can pick up another quest called Bloodscalp Ears from Kebok in Booty Bay. You have to collect 15 ears from the same mobs that give you the tusks. It makes it more worthwhile when you can do 2 quests at the same time. Gives about 2000 xp.

Charms are usually available at the AH. Don't select a catagory, just type in "charm" and search. Usually a few will come up for around 25-50s each. Might take several visits to get them all.

As previously mentioned, liferoot is readily available at the AH. It is also all around where the quest is given, so if you can get a hold of an herbalist, he can pick up 4 or 5 in a few minutes right along the river bank.
replies: I'm adding directions for finding Kebok because it took me so much time to find him.  From the Griffin Stop, go down the stairs in the Griffin building, come out the door and make an immediate left (you can't see the path until you get near the edge because it's such a steep descent).  Follow the path and you'll bump into him when you enter the building (there are no other options as long as you don't jump over the side)

comments.body:
I beat up on the withervine beasts in Dustwallow marsh for an hour and not a single liferoot dropped.  I even saw liferoot growing in the area.  I accidentally found the similarly looking beast in northwest Swamp of Sorrows dropped liferoot.  I got all I needed there.  "Withervine beast" is a bit of a misnomer.  There are several 'swamp beasts' with 'withervine' in the front of their name.  None of them dropped liferoot for me.

Bloodscalp tusks are obtained from the trolls of that name in the northwest corner of Stranglethorn Vale.  Head northwest of Nesingwary's Encampment.

Guys, if you want to take down the trolls go to stranglethorn vale, northeast of Grom Gol base camp just west of Nestingwarrys Expd. you will find a nice grouping of level 33-34 Trolls. The drop rate is like 1-2.

The hard part is naturally the charm farming. 8 of each are needed, [item=4480], [item=4479] and [item=4481].

I was able to [i]solo farm[/i] the mobs needed for the charms at level 36, as Arms warrior, but it was tight. You will almost die on every single one, so bring lots of food.
Buffs of different kinds are highly recommended if you want to attempt to solo them at that level. You can probably do it at level 35 as well if you only go after the level 38 mobs.

Some solo thoughts:
Each mob has their own difficulty. [npc=2761] will slow you and your attack speed, [npc=2762] is also a caster so you can't run away as easily, and [npc=2760] just does a lot of damage. They are not affected by bleeds so [spell=772] is out. [spell=1160] is highly recommended. As an escape you always have [spell=26141], so use that and run if you need to reset. I just used simple [spell=25710] spam while keeping buffs/debuff up, as I found that using [spell=12862] worked poorly due to channeling pushback.

If you can group for them then do so. The other person(s) can take the various elemental parts they drop as rewards, as those can fetch a nice price on the AH.
replies: Can confirm. Possible to solo. Was there as lvl 35 and killed a few until my guildmates joined. Ask for help. If you are 2-5 Players you can even do this at Level 30+, right when you get the quest. There is always lots of players at the spawn place for the Boss as well, that can help to kill him. Just go there and wait for someone who also needs the quest.

The quest is given at lvl 30 but is not doable alone untill 40ish. The elementals are pretty hard at lvl 38-39 not to mention the 40 elite creature you have to kill for the heart. I finnished the quest at lvl 38 with the help of another 38 warrior + a healer for the elite (not neaded though). 

However, you are able to use the weapon you recieve from the quest at the time you get it (30). You should therefor get a highlvl friend to help you collect the tusks and see if u can buy the charms at AH (or your friends help you with that as well) Then kill the elite and have a weapon as good as any lvl 44 green one at lvl 30. U will kick ass! 

I just hope they get a quest like this one at lvl 50 where you get the arcanite champion or another great sword.

If you have the time and/or the money, this is easy. 
Sure, there's no buying the tusks, but you can make it go faster. I went to the Zuuldaia Ruins, just South of the Zul'Kunda Ruins. There were some good 36+ trolls there. An hour and a half, 30 tusks. Combined with the quest Bloodscalp Ears from Booty Bay, and you have yourself a good time with even more xp.

For the Liferoot, I was walking in the Darkmoon Faire, and one of the ladies was selling two. I picked 'em up immediately. Then I bought a stack of Liferoot from the Auction House, picked what I needed, and sold the rest back.

The charms were a bit harder. The Thundering Exiles and the Burning Exiles were easy to kill with a Priest by me, but solo at lower than 35, and you might have some trouble. Bring a friend.

[b] My advice: Buy the Cresting Charms. They are rare, and I am not patient. [/b]

More good tips:

Combine this with other quests, such as the Singing Blue Shards and Bloodscalp Ears, or the Haunted Isle/Water Elementals. Kill many birds with one stone. 

Watch out for Horde if you are an Alliance on a PVP server. It is close to Grom'Gol and there are usually level 60's running around.

Soloing is usually the best for the tusks unless they are too high for you. Good xp, plus some cloth.

Liferoot grows along the river banks near the quest giver.

They respawn quickly (Bloodscalps). Watch out.

Have fun, 
Kaydaa.

My lvl 37 warrior tried to solo cyclonian, because I was dumb and didn't check here first to see that he is elite.  Anyway, I wiped and went to go abandon the quest . . . but it wasn't in the log.  Freak out ensues.  "What!  I'm gonna have to collect all those items again!  What a pain in the <bleep>!"

Well, I have the cosmos/khaos addons and was looking in that PartyQuest log.  When I just looked at the regular log by clicking on the quest log tab at the bottom of my screen, it was there and I could abandon it.  Yippee!

Just wanted to put that out there in case any of you freak about having to re-try the last part of the quest.  You can abandon and re-do without having to get all that stuff again.  Just avoid the khaos version of the quest log since that is currently bugged on the failed quests.

There is one point that can't be made enough here... while it may be possible to purchase these charms; use and ALT or friend to acquire them or even other means; the grind gets you two things:

- XP

- Elemental Fire, Water and Air

Even if you don't need these items, there are plenty of Alchemist, Herbalists and Enchanters who do.

If you need the cash, this is a great way to get it; and to validate my point... you'll find plenty of folks doing the grind on nearly any elemental area. Good luck!

[b]Here's my honest advice: do not bother.[/b] The weapon is only cutting edge for 5 levels, and you may not even [i]get[/i] to Chillwind Point until you are level 31. That has definitely been the case for the last two warriors that I have leveled (both in Classic)... so that's already one utility level gone. Even with the help of a 60, [i]you're going to waste a solid 90 minutes to 2 hours [/i]flying around doing the various parts - in some cases, depending on how lucky you are with your elemental drops, it may be much longer (the elementals in Arathi are a) heavily farmed, and b) have a long [5-10+ minute] respawn rate).

And, of course, this assumes that you have a 60 buddy or two that is willing to contribute that kind of time and effort for a quest with such fleeting returns. If you're thinking of doing this legit - like solo - you might as well just refuse the breadcrumb on Fray Island, because you won't have a prayer of finishing until 38 or 39, at which point the entire exercise is meaningless (unless, of course, you feel that this is a necessary part of your 'warrior experience' [I do not]).

Quests in vanilla/classic that circle-jerk you around the world map should be dropped from the outset. The designers of the original game intended questing to be a facilitator to mob grinding (that is why so many quests have an obnoxiously long and frustrating random component) - the quest experience itself is intended to merely be a cherry on top, not the meat and potatoes of the leveling experience. When you add a 'world tour' on top of that grind, you're just hurting your progress towards 60. 

Now, as I said, maybe that's an experience that you feel like you [b]must[/b] have. But it's definitely not on the menu for me.

*Edit* Something else to consider is that you may be looking at the slow speed of these weapons and thinking "oh, man, BUT THAT'S TOO GOOD TO MISS!" Except, warriors don't even get their first true instant - whirlwind - until level 36 (overpower is an instant, but it's also unpredictable - and if you're fury [and, at this point, lacking tactical mastery] you're probably spending most of your time in berserker and not even using overpower) - so weapon speed doesn't really matter all that much until 36 and 40 (40 being when you should pick up your level 31 talent skill of arms or fury).

This means that the slow speed of these weapons isn't really as advantageous as it seems. In fact, when you are still incredibly reliant on heroic strike and cleave for the majority of your damage output, slow speed can actually HURT YOU (because it makes misses more costly, and rage generation less predictable). [b]Thus, the weapons themselves are overrated for the realities that a level 30-35 warrior is facing in terms of skills available. [/b]
